name: goap_packaged_loop_arbitrary_target
mechanism: Supersedes the 'fixed target only' limitation noted in goap_packaged_loop_increment_to_ten.meta.json. User proposed 3 options for binding an effect-only variable; identified that option 1 (goal-regressive unification) doesn't fit this engine's architecture (plan_facts in hosts.rs is FORWARD uniform-cost search from the start state, not backward Prolog-style goal regression -- there's no single 'current goal' node to unify an effect against mid-search), but option 2A (make Target a genuine PRECONDITION by asserting an explicit target_goal(Id,Target) fact in the world state) requires zero engine changes and matches the engine's real binding mechanism (ground_action_instances only binds via precond-vs-world-state unification). Tested and confirmed working.
user_proposed_fix: "Move Target into the Precondition Context ... Maintain the target state as an explicit ground fact in the world state before planning starts ... Because Target now appears in a precondition (target_goal), your precondition-matching step will successfully bind Target." -- option 2A of 3 proposed; confirmed as the one that fits the actual (forward-search) architecture.
given_background: Primitive 'increment' (precond counter(Id,X)+succ(X,X2); effects swap X for X2) plus succ(X,X2) chain -- same given background as increment_to_ten.
action_definition: action_add("increment_to_target", [["counter",["Id","X"]], ["target_goal",["Id","Target"]]], [["counter",["Id","Target"]]], [["counter",["Id","X"]]], 1) -- Target now appears in a precondition (target_goal), so it binds via ordinary precond-matching, no engine change.
visible_verification: Raw 'increment' (no shortcut) reaches ANY target from ANY start in exactly (target-start) steps across VARYING pairs: (0,5), (2,8), (3,3) [zero-step case], (1,10) -- not just varying start against one fixed target as before.
blind_verification: (start=4, target=12), held back, resolved in exactly 8 steps using only the raw primitive.
acid_test: Two brand-new, never-tested (start,target) pairs -- (2,9) and (6,15), DIFFERENT targets, not just different starts -- both resolved via the single packaged 'increment_to_target' action bound through target_goal, not unrolled raw steps.
verification_status: CORRECTED -- see correction_2026_07_25 below. Original 'verified' status overclaimed.
correction_2026_07_25: A follow-up battery testing this SAME action shape against a structurally different (non-linear, 'doubling') chain exposed that 'increment_to_target'/'decrement_to_target'/'double_to_target' as defined here do NOT verify reachability at all. The action's precondition only requires SOME counter(Id,X) fact and SOME target_goal(Id,Target) fact to both exist -- it unconditionally teleports to Target regardless of whether Target is actually reachable from X via the real underlying primitive/chain. Concrete counter-example: with only double(1,2), double(2,4), double(4,8) as background (6 is NOT reachable from 1 by real doubling), plan([[counter,[unreachable,6]]]) still returned a 1-step plan (double_to_target(Id=unreachable,X=1,Target=6)) -- a FALSE POSITIVE. The earlier increment/decrement acid tests only looked correct because every (start,target) pair tested happened to be genuinely reachable by construction (linear +1/-1 chains reach every intermediate value) -- the action itself provides no such guarantee and was never actually exercising the underlying chain to confirm reachability. This is the exact vacuous-generalization failure mode this whole initiative has been guarding against (see patlang-registry-vs-reference-split), and it slipped through here because the negative/unreachable case was never tested until the follow-up battery. CONCLUSION: target_goal-as-precondition (option 2A) is a valid, zero-engine-change technique for BINDING a variable from world state, but is NOT by itself a correct way to package a verified loop for an arbitrary target -- it needs an additional check that Target is genuinely chain-reachable from X (e.g. a real precondition requiring a 'reaches(X,Target)' fact/relation independently established via the base chain, not just 'a target was declared'). That stronger version has NOT yet been built or verified.
provenance: direct response to user's own proposed engineering options for fixing the earlier-discovered engine limitation (see goap_packaged_loop_increment_to_ten.meta.json's engine_limitation_discovered field) -- evaluated all 3 proposed options, correctly identified option 1 as architecturally mismatched to this codebase's actual forward-search planner, then built option 2A -- which worked mechanically but was NOT sufficiently verified before being marked 'verified' (see correction above).
scope_note: Binding Target via a target_goal precondition fact genuinely works AS A BINDING MECHANISM (no engine change needed) but does not by itself guarantee the resulting single-step plan reflects something actually achievable by the real underlying chain/primitive -- see correction_2026_07_25.
related: spec_library/synthesized_registry/goap_packaged_loop_increment_to_ten.meta.json (the fixed-target precursor -- NOT subject to this flaw, since its target was a ground constant, not a value skipped-past reachability checking), spec_library/synthesized_registry/goap_packaged_loop_decrement_to_zero.meta.json (also not subject to this flaw, same reason), spec_library/synthesized_registry/goap_multi_example_composition.meta.json
